title: Stewardship handoff playpad and midweek watch slate - Dec 2026 (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This document is a working playpad for the midweek small-batch launch lane. It focuses on the stewardship handoff, an hourly watch slate for the 48-hour window, a lightweight heatbench traffic plan, and a concise release notes draft for customer/CS ops. Use as the single-source checklist during the watch shift.

Scope:
- Small feature rollout (feature flag + routing rule for model-variant B) to 5% of global traffic focused on web API.
- Non-breaking path: traffic zipper strategy with staged prefix-shed + KV warmup.
- Target window: Wednesday 09:00 PT -> Friday 09:00 PT (48 hours). Midweek lane to reduce support burden and overlap with core engineering hours.

Quick synopsis (one-liner):
Deploy routing change that sends a 5% cohort to model-variant B with on-path KV prefetch; observe latency and hallucination score metrics; abort or scale-back if signal thresholds exceed defined gates.

Preflight checklist (T-72 -> T-1):
T-72: announce in #deploys, link runbook, confirm on-call rotation. Verify PRs merged and infra green.
T-48: run synthetic smoke against staging (end-to-end). Record baseline latency, error rate, token-cost-per-call.
T-36: heatbench plan loaded: prepare synthetic QPS script, 50% synthetic QPS ramp over 30m, sustained 20m soak.
T-24: data plane snapshot captured (routing rules, model versions). KV cache snapshot exported.
T-12: run canary in pre-prod with 0.5% real traffic for 1h. Check KV hit-rate, cold-start latencies.
T-2: confirm alert routing (PagerDuty escalation path) and on-call names in the watch roster.
T-0: flip feature flag to 5% cohort. Minimum 2 engineers + 1 SRE present for first 2hrs.

Stewardship handoff notes (who does what):
- Release steward (owner): Priya Desai — primary comms, maintains this doc, executes feature flag flip.
- SRE lead: Jonah Park — monitors infra signals, runs fallback if infra errors spike.
- Observability steward: Aisha Khan — verifies dashboards, runs ad-hoc traces, curates signal scores.
- Product owner: Elena Martinez — monitors customer-impact signals and CS queue.

Midweek hourly watch slate (first 8 hours):
Hour 0 (T+0 to T+1): confirm feature flag at 5%, check live KV hit-rate (target > 70%), p50/p95 latency within +20% of baseline, error rate < 0.1%.
Hour 1: run heatbench ramp step 1: add synthetic 25% QPS to cohort for 15m, verify backpressure metrics.
Hour 2: inspect semantic-quality eval snapshots (automated prompt set) for regression; if quality degrade > 3 points, hold.
Hour 3: escalate summary to #deploys and draft initial release notes (see below).
Hour 4: run heatbench soak for 20m at 50% synthetic QPS; confirm token cost delta and tail latency behavior.
Hour 6: check for customer-facing errors and CS tickets; product to triage any P1 reports.
Hour 8: consider bump to 10% only if all signals green and agreement from steward + SRE lead.

Signal gates (abort/scale-back criteria):
- Infrastructure: sustained error rate > 0.5% for 5m OR p99 latency > 3x baseline for 5m => immediate scale-back to 0%.
- Quality: automated eval regression > 4 points on gated prompt set OR manual CS escalations showing reproducible issues => pause and revert cohort to 0%.
- Cost: token-cost-per-call delta > 40% sustained for 30m without clear latency/quality improvement => consult infra/product to decide.

Rollback & fallback matrix (quick steps):
1) Immediate rollback to 0%: steward triggers feature-flag rollback, confirms traffic routing reverts, notifies SRE and product.
2) If rollback fails (flagging system degraded): execute emergency routing policy from 'tiered-fallback' doc (route to model-variant A+quantized).
3) Post-rollback checklist: collect logs, mark timeline in incident channel, create retro ticket.

Heatbench traffic plan (short):
- Aim: expose cold-cache and batching characteristics without servicing live customers.
- Script: synthetic-client jittered requests replaying a curated 30-min production-like trace (small prompts + long prompts mix 70/30).
- Ramp: 0% -> 25% -> 50% synthetic QPS across first 4 hours then soak 20m at 50% if green.
- Monitoring: KV hit-rate, batch sizes, GPU utilization, queue depth, per-model token cost.

Observability quick links (dashboards to keep open):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 by route and model variant.
- Errors: 5xx/4xx split, rate of generator exceptions, OOM events.
- Quality: automated eval scoring, hallucination flags, rerank delta.
- Cost: tokens-per-call, GPU-user-seconds.
- Telemetry: trace sampler for requests failing above p95.

Release notes draft (short, customer-facing):
Title: Rolling out a targeted routing variant to improve throughput efficiency
Summary: On Dec XX we will begin sending a small percentage of web API requests to an updated model routing variant (B). This change aims to reduce median token cost while preserving response quality for conversational and completion endpoints.
What changes for customers: No action required. A small subset of traffic will be evaluated under the new routing and caching logic. You may see slightly different phrasing in rare responses as we validate quality. If you experience degraded output, please contact support with request IDs.
Rollout plan: Gradual 5% to 10% over 48 hours with automatic rollback gates.
Contact: support@redwood.ai and your CSM.

Notes to self / open questions (rough):
- Should we include a short A/B snippet in the API response header for easier debugging? (pro: easier triage, con: header bloat).
- Confirm if KMS rotate window overlaps with this week (Elena to confirm).
- Need a post-deploy evaluation ticket: link to automated eval results and human-review sample set.

Post-deploy retro prompts (to fill after watch window):
- What surprised us?
- Which gate thresholds were conservative/too conservative?
- Any steps we can automate (heatbench startup, auto-annotate failing traces)?
- Action items and owners for next midweek lane.

Quick appendices (short snippets):
- PD escalation list: primary (Jonah Park), secondary (Elena Martinez), tertiary (Aisha Khan).
- Command snippets: 
   * Feature flag rollback: /ff toggle routing-model-b false --env=prod --cohort=all
   * Emergency traffic drain: /routes set-weight modelB 0 --region=global

End of playpad. Keep this doc open during the watch shift. Update timestamps as changes happen and add links to any incident tickets created.

Draft history:
- 2026-12-01: initial sketch (Priya)
- 2026-12-03: added heatbench plan + hourly slate (Aisha)
- 2026-12-05: updated gates and release note draft (Jonah)
